text.p: -- Paribas analyst William Beavington said on Wednesday he had raised his rating for Telefonos de Mexico, or Telmex, to fairly valued - no action, or hold, from overvalued.
-- Beavington also said he had raised his estimates for 1997 earnings per American Depositary Receipt (EPADR) to $3.33 from $2.55 and for 1998 EPADR to $3.94 from $3.41.
-- The upgrade and EPADR increase estimates follow the Mexican government's approval last month of an increase in Telmex's local rates.
-- Beavington told Reuters the rate increase probably incorporated tariff rises that had been expected for 1998. Telmex, a private monopoly until Jan 1, now faces competition.
-- "The Mexican government clearly wants to encourage investment in the local networks," he said.

-- Beavington added that he expected a "short-term upside" for Telmex stock over the next several weeks, or until April 1. Telmex then will face competition in Mexico City, the country's biggest market.
-- "Between now and then it will outperform, and after that it will underperform," he said.
-- Telmex was up one to 37-1/4 in heavy trade in New York.
